text: Contesting the safety rationale offered for restricting Uber, the authors argue that the two way rating system and the algorithmic matching of drivers and customers already provide an effective means of policing drivers and ensuring a safe ride.
citation: Mark Fenwick, Wulf A. Kaal, Erik P. M. Vermeulen, Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2834531

isBasedOn.name: Regulation Tomorrow What Happens When Technology Is Faster Than the Law

abstract: The two–way rating system (drivers rate customers and customers rate drivers) and an algorithm–based system for matching up drivers and customers appear to offer an effective means of policing Uber drivers and ensuring a safe ride for customers.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: ride hailing platforms with reciprocal ratings and algorithmic matching
